messages:
incidents-bot: Pager duty alert — svc-rate high error rate (prod). Symptoms: surge in 5xx from rate-limiter and upstream redis connection resets. Possible third-party cache provider (RedisCloud) connection evictions. Link: <https://pager.example/incident/RC-98765> 

sre_jamie: I'm paged, oncall responding. Looking at rate-limiter logs now. Seeing lots of `ERR connection reset` and `socket closed` from redis client.

alex: I'm online for infra. Can we put rate-limiter into a local fallback cache while we investigate? Quick plan: flip to in-memory token bucket on a subset of pods, then scale if stable.

nina: +1 — also recommend temporarily loosening strict quota enforcement for low-risk routes to reduce customer-facing 429s while we stabilize.

platform-ops: We have standby cluster `redis-standby-2` in a different AZ. Option to switch host for rate-limiter. Provider status page shows networking flaps in eu-west. I've opened a ticket with RedisCloud (case RC-98765).

sre_jamie: Posting relevant log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T21:03:12Z rate-limiter[svc-rate] WARN redis: connection error: read tcp 10.0.12.45:6379: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T21:03:12Z rate-limiter[svc-rate] ERROR token_store: failed get token: redis: nil
2026-03-15T21:04:03Z rate-limiter[svc-rate] METRIC errors: 5xx=128, 429=342
```

alex: Executing controlled failover — patching deployment to point to standby cluster for 3 pods first: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/ratelimiter REDIS_HOST=redis-standby-2 --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout status deploy/ratelimiter -n prod
```

nina: While rollout is in progress, I'm ramping down the strict token consumption for heavy routes: `TOKEN_ALLOWANCE=0.6` and enabling short-term local cache TTLs. That should reduce cache misses.

customer-success-maya: Heads up — external monitoring shows spike in 429s for several customers (CompanyA, CompanyB, OrgC) starting ~21:00 UTC. I'm drafting notifications. Impact level currently P2 (partial degraded service) — billing and webhook delivery affected for CompanyA.

sean: Authz cache also spiking miss rate — `authz_cache.miss_rate` up 12x in eu-west. Could be the same Redis problem or separate. If we fail open auth checks, risk is increased permissiveness. Need product signoff.

nina: We will make auth checks soft-fail for non-critical endpoints for 10m while we stabilize. Implementing a targeted flag: `AUTHZ_FAIL_OPEN=true` for ratelimiter and auth-proxy in eu-west.

platform-ops: RedisCloud responded: "Investigating connection churn in eu-west-1; clients experiencing short TCP resets during rebalancing. Recommended client-side backoff and connection pooling tuning." They've assigned SE contact.

sre_jamie: Failover to standby completed for 3 pods, observing drop in 5xx. Monitoring shows 5xx back to baseline within 90s on those pods. 429s reduced but still higher than normal for bursty keys.

alex: Next action: enable prefix-level local caching for hot keys and increase local bucket capacity. Command I'm applying: 
```
kubectl patch configmap ratelimiter-config -n prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"LOCAL_CACHE_TTL":"15s","HOT_KEY_THRESHOLD":"100"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/ratelimiter -n prod
```

sre_jamie: Metrics update after changes: overall 5xx dropped from 2.3% -> 0.2% in last 10m; 429s decreased from 4.7% -> 1.1% overall. EU region still at ~2.8% 429s.

customer-success-maya: I've sent initial customer notice to CompanyA & CompanyB explaining we're mitigating a third-party cache provider incident; support is triaging customer flows.

sean: Confirming authz soft-fail doesn't apply to org-admin endpoints — we kept strict checks for sensitive routes. Good compromise.

platform-ops: Provider indicates ongoing rebalancing — ETA unknown. We should keep standby routing in place and prepare rollback if standby degrades.

nina: Post-mitigation checklist: 1) Standby routing applied 2) Local cache + TTLs increased 3) Authz soft-fail for low-risk endpoints 4) Customer notifications sent 5) Provider ticket opened. Any missing?

alex: Add: increased connection pool and backoff parameters on redis client before full rollback. Config applied.

sre_jamie: Observability notes for handoff — dashboards to watch: `rate_limiter.5xx`, `rate_limiter.429`, `authz_cache.miss_rate`, `redis.conn_errors`. Alert thresholds lowered to catch regressions (alert on 5xx > 0.5% for 5m).

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled — @alex will take night oncall from 23:00 UTC. Please review runbook: <https://runbooks.example/rate-limiter-redis-failover>. Handoff notes appended.

alex: Acknowledged taking handoff. I'll keep standby routing active until provider confirms stability or until 07:00 UTC tomorrow.

customer-success-maya: I'll follow up with customers in 30m with status update.

sre_jamie: Closing summary for the thread: root cause appears to be RedisCloud network churn causing connection evictions -> token store errors -> rate-limiter 5xx and 429s. Mitigations: partial failover to standby cluster, local in-memory cache fallback, authz soft-fail for non-critical endpoints, client connection/backoff tuning. Provider case RC-98765 open. Next: monitor and prepare for full migration if needed.

oncall-bot: Thread locked for new replies during handoff. If anything critical occurs, page oncall immediately. :rotating_light:
